Applications are open for three new important AI safety positions in New York’s government.

Housed within NY’s Department of Financial Services, the newly created Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity & Trust (DIGIT) will operate as NY’s AI regulator and implement the recently enacted Responsible Artificial Intelligence Safety & Education (RAISE) Act (one of the most important frontier AI laws enacted in the US). DIGIT is equipped with a $9M budget and is now hiring for three roles critical to implementing the RAISE Act:

	*<https://www.dfs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/10/ass_counsel_ns_20261130_0.pdf|Associate Counsel>*
The Associate Counsel “addresses legal issues related to [the RAISE Act],” provides “analysis and counsel” on proposed regulations and legislation, and “formulates legal and policy recommendations.” Preferred qualifications include “four years of relevant professional legal experience,” and experience in AI governance, cybersecurity, or data privacy.
*Salary:* $120,471 - $152,238 (commensurate with experience), with an additional $4,150 if you work from the NYC area
	*Position type:* Full-time, permanent

	*<https://www.dfs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/10/data_ana_3_sg27_20261130.pdf|Data Analyst 3>*
The Data Analyst 3 coordinates “the assessment of data from RAISE Act submissions,” “translates technical details from RAISE Act filings and related information into… reports and briefings for attorneys, policymakers, and operational team members,” “leads technical discussions with frontier model developers,” and “supervises a team of subordinate staff.” Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree plus 5 years of data or modeling experience (or another combination of education and experience). “Preferred qualifications include “working proficiency in SQL and Python or R,” and “advanced knowledge of frontier AI evaluation, security, and safety practices.”
*Salary:* $111,708 with periodic increases up to $137,590, with an additional $4,150 if you work from the NYC area
	*Position type:* Temporary, but likely to become permanent

	*<https://www.dfs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/10/data_analyst_2_sg23_20261130.pdf|Data Analyst 2>*
The Data Analyst 2 “produces business intelligence solutions by querying data from RAISE Act submissions,” “devises methods for identifying data patterns and trends,” “drafts new functions or applications,” and “creates written reports and effectively communicates/presents results.” Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree plus 3 years of data or modeling experience (or another combination of education and experience). “Preferred qualifications include “foundational skills in SQL… and Excel,” “exposure to Python or R,” and “familiarity with frontier AI concepts.”
*Salary:* $90,582 with periodic increases up to $114,585, with an additional $4,150 if you work from the NYC area
	*Position type:* Temporary, but likely to become permanent


The roles can be performed from Albany or NYC, and *applications are due Monday, 11/30*. (The job description for the Associate Counsel role says that it closes on 11/20, but we have been informed that this is a typo.)

*Secure AI Project thinks these are important opportunities for folks who want to contribute to frontier AI policy and help ensure that implementation of the RAISE Act goes well.*

If you’re interested in applying, we encourage you to email <mailto:implementation@secureaiproject.org|implementation@secureaiproject.org>, as we can give more context on the roles. Feel free to forward this to candidates you think may be a good fit!

> • Technical details of AI training and inference

*New members of Congress are hiring staff right now, and people who understand AI risk should apply.* 

The midterms elected 100+ new House members and 18 new senators. They hire their staff between now and March, and the people they hire for tech policy will shape what Congress does on AI next year. Very few applicants will know much about AI safety.

If you’re a US citizen (or a permanent resident applying for citizenship) and could work in person in DC:
1. Read the guide from Citizens for Safe AI: <https://congress.safeai.org/go/guide|congress.safeai.org/go/guide> 
2. Put your resume in the official House and Senate resume banks, and in the pipelines for the party you’d work for. Start with the new members from your home state.
3. Tell the organizers where you applied, so people already on the Hill can recommend you: <https://congress.safeai.org/go/form|congress.safeai.org/go/form> 
Several resume banks close in the next week, so do it now. If you know someone who’d be good at this, please send it to them.

<http://FAR.AI|FAR.AI> is hiring research scientists for our new Applied White-Box Methods team, plus 23 open roles across <https://www.far.ai/careers|other teams> :rocket:

The team will evaluate and develop white-box techniques in realistic settings, like monitoring for agentic coding and training interventions that prevent misalignment learned during RL. The goal is to bridge the gap between curiosity-driven interpretability research and real-world deployment: figuring out which methods actually work in which situations, then using that to improve them and build new ones. That means standard methods like NLAs, activation oracles and J-lens, plus newer ones, tested on large-scale realistic model organisms with probes and black-box monitors as baselines. As the model organisms scale up, the team will also work on white-box AI control and safety cases.

Lots more in the <https://www.far.ai/careers?ashby_jid=8ddbd19c-6d89-4f9e-b879-ab8a369c81b4|job description>. (Note that compensation is negotiable for highly-qualified candidates.)

We’ll also be at the MATS career fair this evening! Jason, who leads our white-box team, and a couple of other researchers will be there, so come say hi :slightly_smiling_face:

From SPAR:
> :loudspeaker: *Mentor applications for SPAR Spring 2027 are open! Submit your project proposal by November 30 (AoE).*
> 
> <https://sparai.org/?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=spar-s27-mentor|SPAR> is a three-month, flexible, fully remote fellowship where experienced professionals and talented students work with experts on AI safety projects, including technical research, policy, strategy, communications and generalist work.
> 
> By participating, mentors get a team of capable collaborators and funding for compute and other project expenses, and orgs are increasingly hiring directly from SPAR. Over 6,000 people from around the world applied last round!
> 
> This round we’re especially keen on projects focused on misalignment science, AI policy, macrostrategy and AGI preparedness, AI incident detection in the real world, communications and public understanding, and AI character and model values. We’re also opening SPAR up to more types of projects, including ones not focused on research. We’re excited to host more strategy, communications, fieldbuilding and generalist projects (see last round’s <https://sparai.org/projects/f26/?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=spar-s27-mentor|here>).
> • *Who we’re looking for*: people working on reducing risks from advanced AI who have a sharp theory of change. No prior mentorship experience needed.
> • *Hosting as an organization*: your org can apply once and host several projects. Fellows can work with more than one person on your team, part-time or full-time, and you can offer them a stipend if you want. <https://sparai.org/mentors?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=spar-s27-mentor#organizations|Apply as an org>.
> • *SPAR Senior Fellows:* last round drew a strong pool of senior talent, and mentors selected over 100 experienced professionals for their projects. This round we’re launching SPAR Senior Fellows to attract even more of them, so you can take on more ambitious projects that need senior collaborators.
> • *Time commitment*: flexible, typically 2 to 10 hours/week depending on how many fellows you take and how hands-on you want to be. The round runs February 8 to May 15, 2027, and applications are noncommittal (you only go ahead if you accept fellows).
> 
> :arrow_right: *Submit your project proposal <https://forms.sparai.org/spar/mentor-app?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=spar-s27-mentor|here> by November 30 (AoE) and learn more about mentoring <https://sparai.org/mentors?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=spar-s27-mentor|here>.*
> 
> Fellow applications open December 16. You can sign up <https://forms.sparai.org/spar/interest?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=spar-s27-mentor|here> to be notified.

Hi, my friend Allen is hiring for a few Research Scientist/Research engineer roles for his org Mycelium, with a projected start date of January 2027. This would involve doing technical research to study robust moral values in AI character, with a particular focus on the welfare of neglected beings (eg. animals, digital minds, etc). I think this is a cool opportunity to do work at the intersection of AI safety and animal welfare! <https://www.projectmycelium.ai/careers|projectmycelium.ai/careers>

Besides the <https://ccst.us/senior-ai-fellow-cal-oes/|Senior AI Fellow positions at Cal OES> (which you should apply to if interested!): If you are a current university student or recent graduate, let me know if you would be interested in an internship (not paid by Cal OES) starting in the next few months. CS/ML experience preferred, along with strong written and verbal communication. I’m only just starting to think about internships and should think more about the highest priorities, but I think these would be some useful projects for interns:
• Drafting recurring memos to inform California executive branch agencies working on California AI governance, as well as other state governments, such as New York and Illinois, or federal partners such as DHS and CISA
• Operationalizing ideas for California AI governance and making them implementable, e.g., from <https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FINAL-N-9-26-AI-EO-9.18.26-SIGNED.pdf|EO N-9-26>, <https://secureaiproject.org/california-policy/|Secure AI Project’s “How California can meet the moment on frontier AI safety,”> or <https://sd13.senate.ca.gov/news/press-release/october-20-2026/senator-becker-introduces-first-its-kind-legislation-to-make-ai|State Senator Josh Becker’s proposal to “Authorize CalOES to establish minimum standards for how companies utilize their R&D computing resources,”> though not advocating for particular legislation
• Creating a public compute cluster by coordinating with possible donors of compute, with one goal being to enable Cal OES to conduct in-house AI safety evals and research experiments to better scrutinize safety cases
• Coordinating with AI nonprofits to ensure that there are good AI safety and security standards written on all important topics, and communicating with AI evaluators and RL environment vendors
• Publishing Cal OES blog posts through the <https://www.caloes.ca.gov/office-of-the-director/operations/homeland-security/california-cybersecurity-integration-center/cybersecurity-task-force/|California Cybersecurity Task Force> (visible to the task force, which various AI companies and nonprofits have joined)
• Participating in standards meetings such as the <https://www.incits.org/news-events/press-releases/incits-announces-new-project-for-framework-for-managing-unique-risks-from-frontier-ai|INCITS Framework for Managing Unique Risks from Frontier AI> and <https://www.nist.gov/super-intelligence/nist-ai-consortium|NIST AI Consortium> (time-consuming but we should start some presence)
You should ideally be a U.S. citizen but I can check the exact rules.

> *Archana Vaidheeswaran*  [3:31 AM]
> Hey folks 
> I help run PRISM(<https://prism-research.org/|prism-research.org> ) an AI safety research fellowship, and we’re looking for *mentors for our 2027 cohort.*
> 
> We’re a bit different from other fellowships where we want fellows to drive their agency into their project. I know a lot of folks come from amazing backgrounds and are switching their careers into safety. We want to harness that agency, so we have fellows work in small teams, and hold each other accountable. The mentor guides them but doesn’t have to drive everything.
> We also focus on people who usually get left out like women, and researchers outside the US who don’t have the same access to labs and networks.
> This year, 9 of our 12 teams got papers into NeurIPS workshops and about 60% of our fellows were from underrepresented groups. 
> 
> Mentoring is about an hour a week for 16 weeks, on a research question you already care about. We pay approx 50$/hour for your time 
> Apply: <https://airtable.com/appBASJ7ePy9Suyuv/pag984zjHAK4U0uKS/form|airtable.com/…/form> 
> 
> I’d love to chat with anyone who wants to be involved in PRISM, whether that’s mentoring, helping out some other way or just learning more about what we’re doing. Feel free to DM me with any questions :two_hearts::sparkles: (edited)
